title: Collection of Signatures at Public Place for Parliamentary Petitions
what_it_is: Collection of Signatures at Public Place for Parliamentary Petitions

sections.label: Parliamentary petition signature collection venues
sections.summary: Asks whether Police will favourably consider applications to collect petition signatures in public places, and how citizens can legally sign outside Speakers' Corner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Police will favourably consider an application to collect signatures for the purposes of a Parliamentary petition on any given matter in a public place; and (b) how and at which public venues other than Speakers' Corner can citizens legally make arrangements to sign a Parliamentary petition as the Parliamentary Standing Orders require a physical signature.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Such events can be held at the Speakers' Corner.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: And those who wish to hold such events outside the Speakers’ Corner will have to apply for a permit.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: A Police permit is not required for public assemblies at the Speakers' Corner which meets the conditions set out in the Public Order (Unrestricted Area) Order 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can he please share details on how the Police exercises its discretion in requiring some calls for signatures for the purposes of a petition to go ahead without a permit, while requiring a permit in other instances, and I am referring to episodes outside of the Speakers' Corner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: I think in those cases, it is fact-sensitive.

sections.label: Permit requirements and Police investigations
sections.summary: States permit requirements are set out in the Act, and Police generally act on information received and investigate before deciding actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: On when the permit is or when the permit is not required is clearly set out in the Act provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: As I mentioned, the Police will generally act on information received and conduct investigations before deciding on what actions to take.
